stem: Ananya wants to observe the planet Mars from the roof of her flat in Chennai on a clear, moonless night in December. Mars is above the horizon at 10 p.m. that night, but a tall building to the east blocks part of the sky, and bright streetlights glow nearby. Under which condition will Ananya have the best chance of actually seeing Mars?

options.text: At 10 p.m., looking away from the tall building, after the streetlights are switched off so the sky is dark and the view is open
At any time during the night, because if Mars exists in the sky it can be seen from any place whenever it is dark
At 10 p.m., even though thick clouds cover the sky, because the sky still looks black at night
In the afternoon, because Mars shines brightly enough to be seen during the day from Chennai

teacher.key_rationale: Visibility requires the object above the horizon at the chosen time, a dark clear sky (streetlights off, no clouds), and an unblocked view away from the building; only A satisfies all conditions. B omits the place/horizon condition, C ignores cloud cover, D violates the dark-sky requirement.
